```{r setup, include=FALSE}

# SETUP: DEFAULT BEHAVIORS FOR CODE CHUNKS
# *****************************************************************************
# These settings control how R code chunks behave in your report:
# - echo = FALSE: Don't show the code, just the output
# - message = FALSE: Suppress package loading messages
# - warning = FALSE: Suppress warning messages
# - dpi = 300: High resolution for all plots (publication quality)
# - fig.width/fig.height: Default dimensions for plots in inches
# - dev = 'png': Use PNG device for better font rendering in HTML output
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE,
  dpi = 300,
  fig.width = 8,
  fig.height = 5,
  dev = 'png'
)

# KNOLOGY COLOR PALETTE
# *****************************************************************************
# Use these color variables throughout your report for consistent branding.
# They can be used in ggplot2 with: geom_point(color = kBlue)
# Or with scale_fill_manual(values = c(kAqua, kOrange, kPurple))

# Primary Knology colors
kBlue <- Knology.Blue <- "#266093"                    # Trusted Blue (primary brand color)
kSky <- Knology.Blue.Highlight <- "#7D9BC0"           # Horizon Blue (light accent)
kYellow <- Knology.Yellow.Widget <- "#D8C827"         # Optimistic Citrine (highlight)
kOrange <- Knology.Orange.Widget <- "#F36C3E"         # Radiant Coral (accent)
kGreen <- Knology.Green.Widget <- "#6CA443"           # New Leaf (nature/growth)
kAqua <- Knology.Blue.Widget <- "#00A2AE"             # Ocean (behaviors)
kPurple <- Knology.Purple.Widget <- "#943A80"         # Passion (culture)
kText <- Knology.Blue.Text <- "#002F6C"               # Dark Blue (Headers)
kBlack <- Knology.Black <- "#101820"                  # Black (Body text)
axis.col <- grey(0.8)                                 # Light grey for axes

# Color vector for multi-category plots (use this for 6+ categories)
# Order: Aqua → Orange → Purple → Yellow → Green → Blue
Knology.bar.col <- c(kAqua, kOrange, kPurple, kYellow, kGreen, kBlue)

# LOAD FONTS
# *****************************************************************************
# Ubuntu is used for headers and plot text
# Open Sans is used for body text (via CSS)
# showtext_auto() enables custom fonts in plots
# showtext_opts() sets the DPI for proper rendering in HTML/PNG output
sysfonts::font_add_google("Ubuntu")
sysfonts::font_add_google("Open Sans")
showtext::showtext_auto()
showtext::showtext_opts(dpi = 300)  # Match the DPI setting for proper text scaling

# LOAD REQUIRED PACKAGES
# *****************************************************************************
library(ggpubr)       # Publication-ready plots and statistical comparisons
library(tidyverse)    # Data manipulation and visualization (includes ggplot2, dplyr, etc.)
library(kableExtra)

# SET SEED FOR REPRODUCIBILITY
# *****************************************************************************
# This ensures that any random operations (sampling, simulations) 
# produce the same results each time you knit the document
set.seed(1234)

# DEFINE KNOLOGY GRAPH STYLE
# *****************************************************************************
# This theme removes unnecessary chart elements and applies Knology branding
# Use it by adding "+ graphStyle" to any ggplot
graphStyle <- theme_bw() +
  theme(
    text = element_text(family = "Ubuntu", size = 18),         # Use Ubuntu font, size 18 for all text
    panel.border = element_blank(),                            # Remove border around plot
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(),                        # Remove major gridlines
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),                        # Remove minor gridlines
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent", colour = NA),  # Transparent panel
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent", color = NA),    # Transparent background
    legend.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent"),    # Transparent legend
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 18),                     # X-axis labels size
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 18),                     # Y-axis labels size
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 18, margin = margin(10, 0, 0, 0)), # X-axis title
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 18),                    # Y-axis title
    plot.title = element_text(size = 20, hjust = 0.5),         # Plot title (centered, larger)
    legend.text = element_text(size = 16),                     # Legend text
    legend.title = element_text(size = 18)                     # Legend title
  )

# WRAP LONG AXIS LABELS
# *****************************************************************************
# Wraps labels to a new line after a specified character limit
# Usage: scale_x_discrete(labels = wrap_labels(20))
# Adjust width = number to control where the line breaks

wrap_labels <- function(width = 15) {
  function(x) stringr::str_wrap(x, width = width)
}
```

### Descriptive Statistics

```{r descriptive-stats}

# Detect output format
is_word <- isTRUE(knitr::opts_knit$get("rmarkdown.pandoc.to") == "docx")

# FREQUENCY TABLE FOR CATEGORICAL ITEMS
# *****************************************************************************
# NA rows are dropped before counting.
# Valid N reflects only rows with a response — this matches the N used in means.

cat_cols <- names(mydata)[sapply(mydata, function(x) is.factor(x) | is.character(x))]

freq_table <- lapply(cat_cols, function(col) {
  valid_rows <- mydata %>% filter(!is.na(.data[[col]]))
  valid_rows %>%
    group_by(Response = as.character(.data[[col]])) %>%
    summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(
      Item    = col,
      Valid_N = nrow(valid_rows),
      Pct     = round(n / Valid_N * 100, 1)
    ) %>%
    select(Item, Response, n, Pct, Valid_N)
}) %>%
  bind_rows()

if (is_word) {
  knitr::kable(
    freq_table,
    caption = "Table 1. Response frequencies for categorical items (non-missing only).",
    col.names = c("Item", "Response", "n", "%", "Valid N"),
    align = "llrrr"
  )
} else {
  knitr::kable(
    freq_table,
    caption = "Table 1. Response frequencies for categorical items (non-missing only).",
    col.names = c("Item", "Response", "n", "%", "Valid N"),
    align = "llrrr"
  ) %>%
    kable_styling(
      bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
      full_width = FALSE
    ) %>%
    collapse_rows(columns = c(1, 5), valign = "top")
}


# DESCRIPTIVE STATISTICS TABLE
# *****************************************************************************
# N is the count of non-NA values, matching the logic in the frequency table

numeric_cols <- names(mydata)[sapply(mydata, is.numeric)]

desc_table <- lapply(numeric_cols, function(col) {
  x <- mydata[[col]][!is.na(mydata[[col]])]
  data.frame(
    Variable = col,
    N        = length(x),
    Mean     = round(mean(x), 2),
    SD       = round(sd(x), 2),
    Median   = round(median(x), 2),
    Min      = round(min(x), 2),
    Max      = round(max(x), 2)
  )
}) %>%
  bind_rows()

if (is_word) {
  knitr::kable(
    desc_table,
    caption = "Table 2. Descriptive statistics for numeric variables (non-missing rows only).",
    col.names = c("Variable", "N", "Mean", "SD", "Median", "Min", "Max"),
    align = "lrrrrrr"
  )
} else {
  knitr::kable(
    desc_table,
    caption = "Table 2. Descriptive statistics for numeric variables (non-missing rows only).",
    col.names = c("Variable", "N", "Mean", "SD", "Median", "Min", "Max"),
    align = "lrrrrrr"
  ) %>%
    kable_styling(
      bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
      full_width = FALSE
    )
}
```

### Violin Plot

```{r violin-plot, fig.cap="Figure 1. Violin plot showing distribution across groups."}

# VIOLIN PLOT
# *****************************************************************************
# Violin plots show the full distribution of data
# They combine features of box plots and density plots
# 
# Color assignment: Use first 3 colors from palette for 3 groups
# - For different number of groups, adjust the values in scale_fill_manual()
# - Example with 4 groups: values = c(kAqua, kOrange, kPurple, kYellow)

ggplot(mydata, aes(x = Group, y = Sepal.Length, fill = Group)) +
  geom_violin(trim = FALSE, alpha = 0.7) +            # Main violin plot, semi-transparent
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.1, fill = "white", outlier.shape = NA) +  # Add small boxplot inside
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(kAqua, kOrange, kPurple)) +  # Assign Knology colors
  labs(
    title = "Distribution by Group",                  # Plot title
    x = "",                                            # X-axis label (empty to use group names)
    y = "Value"                                        # Y-axis label
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = wrap_labels(15))+             #avoid over lap by wrapping text
  scale_y_discrete(labels = wrap_labels(15))+
  graphStyle +                                         # Apply Knology theme
  theme(legend.position = "none")                      # Hide legend (redundant with x-axis)
```

### Bar Plot

```{r bar-plot, fig.cap="Figure 2. Bar plot comparing mean values across groups."}
# BAR PLOT WITH ERROR BARS
# *****************************************************************************
# Bar plots show mean values with error bars (typically standard error or confidence intervals)
# Best for comparing averages across categories
#
# First, calculate means and standard errors for each group

bar_data <- mydata %>%
  group_by(Group) %>%
  summarise(
    Mean = mean(Sepal.Length, na.rm = TRUE),
    SE = sd(Sepal.Length, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n())  # Standard Error
  )

# Create the bar plot
ggplot(bar_data, aes(x = Group, y = Mean, fill = Group)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", alpha = 0.8) +          # Create bars from calculated means
  geom_errorbar(                                       # Add error bars
    aes(ymin = Mean - SE, ymax = Mean + SE),          # Error bar limits
    width = 0.2,                                       # Width of error bar caps
    linewidth = 0.5                                    # Thickness of error bars
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(kAqua, kOrange, kPurple)) +  # Assign colors
  labs(
    title = "Mean Values by Group",
    x = "",
    y = "Mean Value"
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = wrap_labels(15))+             #avoid over lap by wrapping text
  scale_y_discrete(labels = wrap_labels(15))+
  graphStyle +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)  # Angle labels if names are long
  )
```

### Box Plot

```{r box-plot, fig.cap="Figure 3. Box plot showing median and quartiles by group."}

# BOX PLOT
# *****************************************************************************
# Box plots show the median, quartiles, and outliers
# The box represents the interquartile range (IQR: 25th to 75th percentile)
# The line inside is the median
# Whiskers extend to 1.5 × IQR
# Points beyond whiskers are outliers

ggplot(mydata, aes(x = Group, y = Sepal.Length, fill = Group)) +
  geom_boxplot(
    alpha = 0.7,                                       # Semi-transparent boxes
    outlier.colour = kText,                            # Color outlier points
    outlier.size = 2                                   # Size of outlier points
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(kAqua, kOrange, kPurple)) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution by Group",
    x = "",
    y = "Value"
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = wrap_labels(15))+             #avoid over lap by wrapping text
  scale_y_discrete(labels = wrap_labels(15))+
  graphStyle +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

### Horizontal Means Plot

```{r means-plot, fig.cap="Figure 4. Horizontal plot of mean values with confidence intervals."}

# HORIZONTAL MEANS PLOT
# *****************************************************************************
# This plot style is useful for:
# - Comparing means across multiple categories with long names
# - Showing ratings or survey responses
# - Displaying knowledge/attitude scales
#
# Calculate means and confidence intervals

means_data <- mydata %>%
  group_by(Group) %>%
  summarise(
    Mean = mean(Sepal.Length, na.rm = TRUE),
    Lower = mean(Sepal.Length, na.rm = TRUE) - 1.96 * sd(Sepal.Length, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n()),
    Upper = mean(Sepal.Length, na.rm = TRUE) + 1.96 * sd(Sepal.Length, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n())
  )

# Reverse the order of categories (top to bottom)
means_data$Group <- factor(means_data$Group, levels = rev(means_data$Group))

# Create horizontal plot
ggplot(means_data, aes(x = Mean, y = Group)) +
  geom_vline(                                          # Add reference line (e.g., midpoint or threshold)
    xintercept = 5.8,                                  # Adjust this value as needed
    linetype = "dashed",
    color = kYellow,
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  geom_errorbarh(                                      # Horizontal error bars
    aes(xmin = Lower, xmax = Upper),
    height = 0.2,                                      # Height of error bar caps
    linewidth = 1,
    color = kBlue
  ) +
  geom_point(size = 4, color = kBlue) +               # Mean points
  scale_x_continuous(
    limits = c(4, 8),                                  # Adjust axis limits for your data
    name = "Value"
  ) +
  scale_y_discrete(name = "") +
  labs(title = "Mean Values by Group") +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = wrap_labels(15))+             #avoid over lap by wrapping text
  scale_y_discrete(labels = wrap_labels(15))+
  graphStyle +
  theme(
    axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),                    # Remove y-axis ticks
    plot.margin = margin(r = 0.75, t = 0.25, unit = "lines")
  )
```

### Grouped Comparison Plot

```{r grouped-means, fig.cap="Figure 5. Comparison across multiple groups and conditions."}

# GROUPED HORIZONTAL MEANS PLOT
# *****************************************************************************
# Use this when you want to compare multiple groups across multiple categories
# Example: Comparing treatment effects across different demographic groups
#
# For this example, we'll create a grouped dataset

# Prepare data with multiple measurements per group
grouped_data <- mydata %>%
  group_by(Group) %>%
  summarise(
    Measure1 = mean(Sepal.Length, na.rm = TRUE),
    Measure2 = mean(Sepal.Width, na.rm = TRUE),
    Measure3 = mean(Petal.Length, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(                                        # Convert to long format for plotting
    cols = starts_with("Measure"),
    names_to = "Measure",
    values_to = "Value"
  ) %>%
  group_by(Group, Measure) %>%
  summarise(
    Mean = mean(Value),
    SE = sd(Value) / sqrt(n()),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Reverse category order for better readability
grouped_data$Measure <- factor(
  grouped_data$Measure,
  levels = rev(c("Measure1", "Measure2", "Measure3")),
  labels = rev(c("Sepal Length", "Sepal Width", "Petal Length"))
)

# Create grouped plot
ggplot(grouped_data, aes(x = Mean, y = Measure, color = Group)) +
  geom_vline(                                          # Optional reference line
    xintercept = 3,
    linetype = "dashed",
    color = grey(0.6)
  ) +
  geom_errorbarh(                                      # Error bars
    aes(xmin = Mean - SE, xmax = Mean + SE),
    height = 0,
    linewidth = 1.5,
    position = position_dodge(-0.5)                    # Offset groups vertically
  ) +
  geom_point(                                          # Mean points
    size = 3,
    position = position_dodge(-0.5)
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(kAqua, kOrange, kPurple)) +  # Color by group
  scale_x_continuous(name = "Mean Value") +
  scale_y_discrete(name = "") +
  labs(title = "Comparison Across Groups and Measures") +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = wrap_labels(15))+             #avoid over lap by wrapping text
  scale_y_discrete(labels = wrap_labels(15))+
  graphStyle +
  theme(
    axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "right",                         # Show legend for group colors
    plot.margin = margin(r = 0.75, t = 0.25, unit = "lines")
  )
```
